producer_report.summary:
I added `check_outcome_state` to reading acceptance. A request that uses publish, deploy, share or release as a verb with a delivery object (page, site, docs, report, a `v1` version, a destination, an audience) is now refused unless a Behavior criterion holds a whole-word state phrase. Examples of state phrases are "reachable", "is served", "HTTP 200" and "downloadable". The other way out is an out_of_scope item that names every detected verb or its -ing form as a whole word. The check is a `step!` in `refusing_check`, right after `check_governance_coverage`. The error names the verbs and says to add a behavior criterion with a reachable URL, a served page or a downloadable release, or to name the delivery out of scope.

**Scope is 1 of the 3 cited jobs.** The request text of all three jobs is in the evidence snapshot's `request.json` files, so the replay test quotes each one verbatim. Run through the gate, only 20261014-082328-g6vy (Publish a first explainer page) is refused. 20261014-174815-7bf8 (ladder of requirements) and 20261017-173508-0wtc (ontology decision) contain no delivery verb. They are another class, outside the check and not caught. The CHANGELOG, the doc comment and D161 say so. The replay test asserts the CHANGELOG states "covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs", says "are not caught", and does not claim "3 of the 3".

**Verifier findings from job 20261027-054230-8nz8:**
- (a) and (b): the claim is narrowed to 1 of 3 and tied to the replay test.
- (c): out_of_scope matches by whole word, so "Changes to shared helpers" and "Release notes are unchanged" do not count. A following word such as "notes" or "button" makes the verb a noun.
- (d): `url`, `tag`, `link`, `page`, `can open` and a bare `available at` are not state phrases. A content-kind criterion with a state phrase does not pass either, because a Grep on a file can meet it.
- (e): verbs are found after `and`, `please`, `can you`, `want to` and similar lead-ins, and after list markers (`-`, `*`, `1.`, `2)`, `(a)`).
- (f): the placement after the governance check is explained in D161, and a corpus case pins the order.

**Technical uses.** A crate, package, binary, app, image or artifact is not a delivery object on its own. "Release the lock", "Share the HTTP client", "Publish the event to the bus", "Share the parsing code between crates" and "Release the image buffer" are accepted.

**Refusal rate.** The 5% is an estimate. The only count I took: 29 of the 1045 recorded request files contain one of the four words anywhere (Grep over the evidence snapshot), mostly as the noun "share". That bounds the real share well below 5%.

**Tests.**
- Seven new unit tests in `reading.rs`.
- The three existing governance tests that send a Publish or Deploy request now carry a Behavior state criterion.
- Fifteen new corpus cases, plus a Behavior criterion on the existing brand-word case.
- Six new input-form tags (17 to 23).
- The replay test `delivery_verb_replay_over_the_cited_jobs`.

I wrote no reader rule, so the reader learns of the check from the refusal text on its re-read. D161 records that cost.

checks_run.note: 1080 lib tests passed (1 ignored), 2 and 12 in the other test binaries, including all refusal_corpus tests.
The READING_RULES brief test (6 entries) passes.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs shows check_outcome_state refusing a reading for the real g6vy request 'Publish a first explainer page on how firstmate handles work.' whose criteria only say a file exists. The error names the missing observable state (reachable URL or served page). The test fails when the check is removed.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core -q` passed (1080 lib tests, 2 and 12 in the other binaries). `check_outcome_state_refuses_the_g6vy_misread` uses the recorded g6vy request with the reading 'docs/explainer.md exists' and asserts the error contains 'reachable URL', 'served page' and 'publish'. It also asserts `refusing_check` returns the name `check_outcome_state`. Without the check, `refusing_check` would return None and the `unwrap` would panic.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. A replay test runs refusing_check over the recorded request text of all three cited jobs (20261014-082328-g6vy, 20261014-174815-7bf8, 20261017-173508-0wtc), asserts the check refuses exactly the real delivery-verb misread (g6vy) and not the other two, and asserts the caught count is 1 of 3.
criteria_check.evidence: `delivery_verb_replay_over_the_cited_jobs` in refusal_corpus.rs passed. CITED_REQUESTS holds the three request texts verbatim, read from the evidence snapshot's request.json files. The test asserts caught == [g6vy], that the other two are accepted, and that the CHANGELOG says 'covers {caught} of the {total} cited jobs', i.e. 1 of 3.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. Unit tests show acceptance when a criterion names a reachable URL or served state, for deploy, share and release as well as publish, and show no refusal for 'Add a timeout setting'. Tests show detection of 'Build the docs and publish them', 'Can you deploy the site' and 'I want to release v1'.
criteria_check.evidence: `check_outcome_state_accepts_a_behavior_state_for_each_delivery_verb` covers publish, deploy, share and release with a Behavior state criterion (accepted), the same text as a Content criterion (refused), and 'Add a timeout setting' (accepted). `delivery_verbs_are_found_after_lead_ins_and_markers` asserts the three lead-in requests are detected, plus bullets, `1.`, `2)`, `(a)` and the technical non-matches. All passed. Corpus cases delivery-verb-after-and, -after-can-you and -after-want-to refuse via check_outcome_state.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. Tests show an out_of_scope item such as 'Changes to shared helpers' or 'Release notes are unchanged' does not satisfy the check for a Share or Release request, and a criterion containing only 'tag' or 'URL' as incidental words (for example 'the <title> tag names the page') does not satisfy it for a publish request.
criteria_check.evidence: `out_of_scope_and_incidental_words_do_not_satisfy_the_check` passed. It asserts 'Changes to shared helpers' (Share request) and 'Release notes are unchanged' (Release request) are refused, and that 'Sharing the report is out of scope' and 'Releasing is out of scope: no tag is cut' are accepted. It also refuses Behavior criteria 'the <title> tag names the page', 'The URL field is documented', 'A reader can open docs/explainer.md' and 'docs/explainer.md is available at docs/' for a publish request. The matching corpus cases pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Grep crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs shows a `step!(check_outcome_state(` line inside refusing_check, with a doc comment naming the root cause (a delivery verb read as a narrow deliverable, with no check against the state the user observes) and stating it covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs (20261014-082328-g6vy), naming the other two as outside the check.
criteria_check.evidence: The line `step!(check_outcome_state(reading, request));` is in refusing_check directly after the governance step. The doc comment above `pub fn check_outcome_state` is one `///` block. It says a delivery verb was read as a narrow deliverable with no check against the state the user observes, and that the check covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs (20261014-082328-g6vy). It names 20261014-174815-7bf8 and 20261017-173508-0wtc as outside the check. Test `check_outcome_state_doc_names_root_cause_and_scope` pins all of this and passed.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`. The corpus has a case in which check_outcome_state refuses and a matching accepting case, and the rule that every step! has a refusing case still passes.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` ran 12 tests, all ok. Twelve new cases are refused by check_outcome_state, and delivery-verb-first-reading-names-a-served-state, delivery-verb-out-of-scope-names-it-accepted, delivery-word-as-a-noun-is-accepted and delivery-verb-technical-use-is-accepted are the accepting ones. `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case`, `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` and `the_wrapper_agrees_with_refusing_check_on_every_case` pass.

criteria_check.criterion: The change refuses more readings. Expected 5% of newly refused readings. A replay of past readings is expected to hold the job only above 10%. The higher refusal rate is intended: the check applies only to requests with a delivery verb whose reading names no observable state.
criteria_check.evidence: The doc comment and CHANGELOG say 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended' and 'expected 5% of newly refused readings', labelled an estimate. `outcome_state_refusal_is_declared_intended` passed: `replay_declaration` parses the share as 5, and it checks the doc and CHANGELOG wording. The only measurement is a Grep count of 29 of 1045 recorded requests containing one of the four words anywhere, which bounds the real share from above. I did not run the verification-time replay.

The new top entry in [Unreleased] / Added names the root cause, `check_outcome_state`, 'covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs' and 'are not caught' for the other two. The replay test asserts that wording. open_issues: The real refusal share was not measured; the verification-time replay will measure it. The 5% is an estimate, and the only count taken is 29 of 1045 recorded request files containing one of the four words anywhere.

Departure from the plan: all three cited request texts were available in the evidence snapshot, so I dropped the stand-in fixtures, the `verbatim` flag and the 'not replayed' wording. The replay is verbatim for all three jobs. The PACKAGE_NOUNS constant is also dropped, since destination and version tokens already count as objects on their own.

Known limits (in the doc comment and D161): other verbs (ship, launch, upload), verbs in comma lists or gerund starts, objects outside the lists, 'reachable' said of a file, and 'Release the page lock' is refused. The other two cited jobs (ladder, ontology) are another class and are not addressed.
I did not run the full `cargo test --locked` over the workspace; Athena's checks do.
mistakes: My first draft of the doc comment had a blank `///` line, which my own pinning test rejects; I removed it before running the tests.
The object-before-verb scan first spanned the previous sentence when the verb opened a segment; I fixed it by starting the scan at the verb in that case.
learnings: The evidence snapshot's records/jobs/<month>/<job>/request.json files hold the exact request text of all three cited jobs, so the replay test quotes them verbatim.
check_code_survey fires only for class_of_work code or tests, so a Behavior state criterion on the docs/feature fixtures needs no code survey.

Package-type nouns (crate, package, binary, app, image, artifact) as object words refuse ordinary Rust requests like 'Share the parsing code between crates'; they count only through a destination or version token, which are objects on their own, so I left them out of the object list.
docs/decisions.md D160 uses 'Amends' and has a link in docs/decision-links.toml; D161 avoids the supersession phrases and names no other decision, so no link is needed.
Bash in this job only allows cargo, git, ls, mv, rm, chmod; large test output cannot be piped to tail and the tool-results file cannot be read, so use `cargo test -q` to keep output short.
desires: A way to run the verification-time replay of accepted readings before handing over, to measure the real refusal share instead of bounding it with a Grep count.
